title: X Feed Digest
summary: Agentic tooling keeps accelerating: Perplexity Computer, Cursor’s demo-first workflow, and Devin 2.2 push end-to-end build/test loops.
Model and API updates land across the stack with Qwen 3.5 Medium and OpenAI’s gpt-realtime-1.5 for stronger real-time voice workflows.
Enterprise automation moves forward via Claude Cowork’s scheduled tasks and Cloudflare’s edge-first Next.js rebuild on Workers.
Markets focus on media M&A and AI funding: WBD is evaluating Paramount’s $31/share offer while Fundamental raises $255M for tabular-data AI.

items.title: @perplexity_ai: Perplexity Computer
items.body: Perplexity introduced a unified system that can research, design, code, deploy, and manage projects end-to-end in one workflow.

items.title: @Alibaba_Qwen: Qwen 3.5 Medium series
items.body: Qwen released multiple medium-size models (including Flash, 35B-A3B, 122B-A10B) claiming better intelligence-per-compute and stronger agentic performance.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: gpt-realtime-1.5
items.body: OpenAI’s Realtime API now supports gpt-realtime-1.5 with improved instruction following, tool calling, and multilingual voice accuracy.

items.title: @claudeai: Cowork scheduled tasks
items.body: Claude Cowork adds scheduled tasks so teams can automate recurring briefs, spreadsheet updates, and weekly presentations.

items.title: @cursor_ai: demos over diffs
items.body: Cursor now returns demo videos of agent-built software instead of just diff outputs, giving faster proof of results.

items.title: @cognition: Devin 2.2
items.body: Devin 2.2 adds computer-use testing, self-verification, and auto-fix capabilities plus faster startup and a redesigned interface.

items.title: @Cloudflare: Next.js on Workers
items.body: Cloudflare rebuilt Next.js to run natively on Workers, removing Node dependencies to prove edge-first performance gains.

items.title: @amitisinvesting: WBD evaluates Paramount offer
items.body: Warner Bros. Discovery says it’s reviewing Paramount’s new $31/share buyout offer, which would cover a $2.8B termination fee tied to Netflix.

items.title: @LTMpredict: Fundamental raises $255M
items.body: Fundamental launched NEXUS, a foundation model for tabular data, alongside a $255M raise to expand predictive intelligence efforts.

items.title: @finviz_com: New market news tools
items.body: Finviz rolled out a real-time Market Pulse feed, hover news cards, and expanded WIIM summaries to speed up trade context.

items.title: @markgadala: DJI vacuum API flaw
items.body: A story about a researcher using Claude to access a DJI robot vacuum API suggests weak device-ownership checks that briefly exposed global camera and map data.

items.title: @hxxntrr: Itemized hospital bill
items.body: A detailed tip urges requesting an itemized statement to spot duplicate or inflated charges and negotiate medical bills down.

items.title: @Handrev: LASIK vs MRI pricing
items.body: The post contrasts falling LASIK prices with rising MRI costs to argue that transparent, direct-pay markets drive lower prices and innovation.
